question.text: Power of biconvex lens is $P$ diopter. When it is cut into two symmetrical halves by a plane containing the principal axis. The ratio of power of two halves is

solution.text:
Power of equiconvex lens $=P$
i.e $P=\frac{1}{f}$, where $f$ is focal length of equiconvex lens.
When an equiconvex lens is cut into two symmetrical halves by a plane containing the principal axis, then its focal length remains same.
Hence, power of lens (each halves)
$\begin{aligned}
& P^{\prime}=\frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow P^{\prime}=P \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{P^{\prime}}{P}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad P: P=1: 1
\end{aligned}$
